D019_m001.question:
I can’t sleep—like, at all. I lie down and my mind just races, and when I do finally drift off, I’m jolted awake by this vivid... memory? It feels like I’m right back in the car. It’s been like this since the accident, which was about a week ago. I was on my way home from a site visit—rainy, dark roads—and this truck ran the light. We crashed. My husband was in the passenger seat. He’s okay, thank God, but I keep seeing it. Like, full-on seeing it. I’ll be standing at the drafting table, and suddenly I hear the screech of tires, feel the impact, and I’m frozen. For a second—or longer—I can’t tell if I’m here or there. I had one during a client meeting. Embarrassing. 

I’ve been avoiding driving, even though my job requires visiting outdoor sites. I’m delegating everything, and that’s not like me. I design spaces meant to feel safe, peaceful—but I can’t even feel safe in my own home. I jump at noises, can’t concentrate on plans, and I’ve lost my appetite. I keep thinking, “If I’d left five minutes later…” It’s like my brain won’t let me move past it. I just want to feel like myself again.
D019_m001.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D019_m002.question:
I’ve been having a really hard time since that night in the kitchen last week—just seven days ago, but it feels longer. There was a fire in the prep area, and one of my line cooks got burned pretty badly right in front of me. I tried to help, but I keep seeing his face… over and over. It just pops into my head—when I’m plating, when I’m driving, even when I’m trying to fall asleep.  

I haven’t been sleeping at all. I wake up around 4:30 every morning, heart racing, like I’m back in it. My wife says I’m distant, but I don’t want to talk about it. I can’t stand being in the kitchen now. Yesterday I called in sick for the first time in years—just couldn’t do it. I keep thinking I failed, that I should’ve moved faster.  

It’s affecting everything. I yelled at my wife for no reason the other day, and I haven’t been able to focus on recipes. I’ve missed two deliveries already. I know it’s only been a week, but I can’t keep working like this. I feel like I’m breaking.
D019_m002.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D019_m003.question:
I’ve been having a real hard time since that incident at work last week—someone pulled a knife on me during a disturbance at the mall. I didn’t think I’d be so shaken up, but ever since then, I can’t seem to quiet my mind at night. I lie in bed for hours, just staring at the ceiling, my heart racing like I’m back in the moment. My wife says I’ve been restless, talking in my sleep, and sometimes I wake up sweating.  

And the dreams... they’re relentless. I keep reliving the scene—same guy, same hallway—but in my dream, it ends worse. I’m on the ground, or my backup never shows. I wake up panicked, gasping. It’s happening almost every night now.  

I’ve been on this job for nearly 20 years and never had anything like this happen so close. I’m jumpy now, even at home. The dog barks and I flinch. I don’t want to go back to work, but I’ve been taking sick days, and I know my captain’s getting worried. My wife keeps asking if I’m okay, but I don’t even know how to explain it. I’m just… not myself.
D019_m003.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D019_m004.question:
I’ve not been right since it happened last week—my son found me on the floor after the fall, but I remember so little. The ambulance ride, the hospital… it keeps coming back in pieces, like I’m there again, hearing the paramedics talk, feeling the cold floor, even though I’m in my chair. It scares me. I don’t close my eyes because I fear I’ll be back on that kitchen tile, unable to move or call for help.  

I can’t sleep at night. I lie down at ten, but my mind races—reliving the moment, wondering what if no one had come. It takes hours to drift off, if at all. Some nights I just give up and sit by the window.  

Since my husband passed, it’s just been me. I manage most days, but this… this is different. I’m jumpy, tearful, and I don’t want to talk to the girls next door anymore. I was always independent—cooking, cleaning—but now I can’t bring myself to make a proper meal. It’s like I’m detached, watching myself from the outside. I know I need help, but I feel so lost.
D019_m004.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D019_m005.question:

I’ve been calling in “sick” when I’m not—can’t face the site. Foreman’s supposed to hold it together. But I feel… cracked. It’s affecting everything—my crew, my marriage, me. I’ve never felt like this before. I don’t want to shut down, but I can’t seem to get back to normal, either.
D019_m005.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D019_m006.question:
I’ve been having a really hard time since... well, it’s been about a week now since the accident. I was driving home late after a crunch week at work—game launches are always hectic, testing bugs until 2 a.m.—and this truck ran the red light. I remember the impact, the sound of glass shattering… but then it gets hazy. I can’t remember how I got out of the car or what the paramedic said when he talked to me. That scares me.  

Since then, I keep waking up every few hours. My mind just races. Even when I’m tired, lying there in the dark, I see the headlights again. It’s like my brain won’t shut off. I’m back in the car, but pieces are missing. I hate that.  

At work, I passed a major test cycle yesterday—one I would’ve been proud of before—but I just felt… nothing. A teammate said, “Great job,” and I nodded, but inside, it was empty. I’ve always lived for clearing those milestones, especially after pulling all-nighters. Now, it’s like the win doesn’t land.  

I’ve been avoiding driving, even rideshares. The thought of being near a street that feels like that intersection? I can’t. I’m missing shifts. My lead emailed me today—concerned. I know I should be fine. It’s just one week. But I don’t feel close to fine.
D019_m006.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D019_m007.question:
I’m a 29-year-old medical resident—third week into my ICU rotation—and I’ve just been in a code that… I can’t really talk about it without my chest tightening. It happened a week ago. A young guy, close to my age, coded after a trauma call. We worked on him for nearly 45 minutes. I keep seeing flashes—blood, alarms, the time of death being called—but whole chunks are just… gone. I don’t remember walking out of the room or changing my scrubs. That scares me more than anything.

Since then, I can’t shake this heavy numbness. My roommate says I’ve been sleeping 12 to 14 hours a day—crashing right after work, even if I nap during the day. I don’t feel tired, just… empty. My friends invited me to dinner last night—something we always do after shifts—but I didn’t go. Nothing feels good anymore. Not food, not jokes, not even finishing my rotation. I just go through motions.

I know I need to function—I’ve got patients, evaluations, my license down the line—but I can’t focus. Every time I close my eyes, I’m back in that room, except I don’t know what actually happened. I just know I was there… and then I wasn’t.
D019_m007.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D019_m008.question:

I don’t… I don’t remember much of what happened during it. One second I was walking, and then—nothing. My next clear memory is someone pulling me behind a car, and my hands were shaking so bad I couldn’t feel them. Now I can’t sleep through the night. I lie down, my body’s tired, but I wake up feeling like I haven’t rested at all—like I’ve been running in my sleep.

At work, I can’t concentrate. I keep re-reading the same file over and over. I had to take a day off because I got panicked just hearing a car backfire outside the office. I’m usually steady under pressure, but this… this feels different. Like I’m not even myself anymore.
D019_m008.options:

    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D019_m009.question:

We lost a young trauma patient—someone I’d been fighting to save for over an hour. I keep replaying pieces of it, but weirdly, there are gaps—like the moment the code was called. I can’t focus at work. I’m making small mistakes—things I’d never usually do. I had to ask a junior nurse to double-check a med dose yesterday. That’s not me. I’ve always been the one others rely on. Now I feel like I’m breaking down, and it’s only been a week. I’m scared to go back on night shift. I just want to feel like myself again.
D019_m009.options:

D019_m010.question:

D019_m011.question:
I’ve been completely off since last week—about seven days ago—when I rear-ended a car during a downpour. Nothing serious, no injuries, but… something just snapped. I keep seeing that moment—the headlights in my mirror, the moment of impact—like it’s burned into my head. I don’t feel like myself.

I used to just grab my gear and hit the road, but now I can’t even decide what shirt to wear. It’s stupid, right? But I stand there frozen. Same with food—used to love diner breakfasts, now I sit staring at the menu like it’s a test I’ll fail. 

And I can’t stop checking. Before I even settle into the truck, I walk around it twice, checking the exits at every stop, watching people too close, making sure nobody’s approaching fast. If someone walks out from behind a fuel pump quick, I jump—heart pounding, hands shaking. My wife said I flinched when she touched my shoulder in the kitchen yesterday. 

I’m not sleeping. I’m driving slower, stopping more, scared of making a wrong move. I’ve never been like this. I’m supposed to be back out Monday, but I don’t know if I can. I can’t keep doing this if I’m this wound up.

    D. Bipolar I Disorder

D019_m012.question:

D019_m016.question:

I can’t talk about it. My union rep wanted me to go to debriefing, but I couldn’t. Just the thought of replaying it makes my chest close up. I’ve been calling in sick, avoiding the yard, even stopped taking the train when I’m off—ironic, I know. I’m a subway driver who can’t ride the subway.

I don’t sleep. When I do, I wake up back there—same sounds, same helpless feeling. I’m not sure I can go back to the booth. I don’t feel like myself.

D019_m024.question:
I just can’t shake it, doctor. It’s been about three weeks since that night—the accident. I was driving home from work, it was raining, and this truck skidded right into my lane. I remember the headlights coming at me, so fast… I still see it when I close my eyes. Since then, anything even close to that moment freaks me out. The sound of tires on wet pavement? I’ll start sweating, my chest tightens. Even the smell of wet asphalt from a car pulling into a parking lot—it hits me like a wave.

I’m not sleeping. When I do, I’m back behind the wheel. I’ve snapped at my team at work for no reason—little things, like a delayed email or a dropped call, and I just explode. It’s not like me. I manage a whole support team; I need to be calm, but now I feel like I’m walking on broken glass all the time. My nerves are raw. One wrong tone from someone, and I’m ready to cry or yell—I don’t even know which. I keep thinking, *What if I hadn’t swerved?* I can’t get it out of my head. It’s like I’m stuck there.
D019_m024.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D019_m025.question:
I’ve been having a really hard time since the car accident three weeks ago. I wasn’t seriously hurt, but the other driver wasn’t so lucky, and I keep seeing it over and over in my head—the sound, the glass breaking, their face. I can’t shake it. I’ve had these awful dreams almost every night since it happened. I’m back in the car, or I’m watching it unfold from outside, and I can’t move, can’t help. I wake up panicked, sometimes crying.

During the day, it’s like I’m not really here. My husband says I’ve been snapping at him for no reason. I didn’t realize how bad it was until I yelled at a student yesterday—six-year-old Emma—because she played a note wrong. She started crying, and I just broke down. I’ve never been like that before. I feel on edge all the time, like something bad’s about to happen, even when I’m just sitting at the piano. I love teaching—it’s been my life—but now I’m dreading it. I keep thinking I don’t deserve to feel this way; I survived, after all. But I can’t seem to pull myself together.
D019_m025.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D019_m026.question:
I, um… look, I don’t really know how to say this. Something happened last week—only about six days ago. I was operating the crane, fifth floor up, hoisting steel beams. One of the riggers made a mistake, and a beam came loose. It didn’t hit me, but it slammed down right next to the tower. A guy on the ground… he didn’t make it. I saw the whole thing. Since then, I can’t… I just can’t steady myself.

Outta nowhere, if someone walks up fast or waves a hand, I jump like I’ve been shocked. My heart goes nuts. Even my wife startled me yesterday just turning on the kitchen light. She said I backed up like she was going to hit me.

And… this sounds weird, but everything feels fake, like a bad movie. The job site looked hazy, like I was watching through glass. Colors don’t seem right. I had to stop working—my boss sent me home after I froze during a lift. I just… didn’t know where I was for a second.

I can’t sleep. When I do, I’m back there. My wife says I talk in my dreams. I don’t want to be around people, but I don’t want to be alone either. I just feel… untethered.
D019_m026.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Binge-Eating Disorder
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D019_m027.question:
I’ve been a taxi driver for 15 years—seen all kinds of things on the road, but nothing like this. Last week, I was taking a fare through the industrial district late at night when two guys with guns jumped in, forced me to drive, made me hand over all the cash. One of them put a gun right in my side. I couldn’t move. I couldn’t think. It felt like the whole world… just stopped. I remember looking at the clock on my dash—7:23—and that number just stuck in my head. I don’t even know how much time passed. Could’ve been minutes, could’ve been hours.  

Since then, I can’t settle. Any loud noise—a horn, a backfire—and my heart starts slamming, my hands shake. I can’t pull myself together after. I’m sweating for ages. I had to stop working. I drove two blocks yesterday and had to pull over, couldn’t breathe. I’m not sleeping. I keep seeing that gun, hearing their voices.  

I’m divorced, no kids at home, so no one’s checking on me. But I can’t do this alone. I feel like I’m losing my mind. That moment—it’s not passing. It’s stuck on repeat.
D019_m027.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Binge-Eating Disorder
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D019_m028.question:

If anything startles me—a door slamming, a phone ringing—I feel like my heart’s going to burst. My hands shake, and it takes me ages to calm down. It’s like my body won’t reset. My coworkers noticed; I dropped a coffee cup during a call because my hands were trembling so bad.  

And the world… it’s like I’m watching everything through a fog. Yesterday, I was sitting in a conference room, and the walls seemed to warp. Everyone’s voices sounded muffled, like I was underwater. It felt like a dream, but not in a good way—like nothing was real. I keep wondering if I’m losing my mind.  

I haven’t been sleeping. I keep seeing that car coming at me. I’m avoiding driving, even though I have to. It’s messing with my work, my focus… I’m barely holding it together. I thought I’d bounce back by now, but it’s just getting worse.
D019_m028.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Binge-Eating Disorder
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D019_m029.question:

I saw him, slammed the controls, but I *thought* I hit him. Turned out he jumped back in time, wasn’t even touched. But in that moment… man, it felt like my body froze. Time just… stopped. Everything slowed down so much it was like watching a tape in slo-mo. I could see every detail—the guy’s face, the sleeve of his jacket ripping as he fell. But it wasn’t real-time. It felt stretched.

Since then, I can’t shake it. I keep seeing it when I close my eyes. My wife touched my shoulder last night to wake me, and I nearly jumped out of my skin—swung my arm, startled her bad. I didn’t even know it was her. I’ve been calling in sick. Can’t go back up there. My hands sweat just thinking about the cab. It’s only been a week, but I’m not sleeping, I’m jumpy, and I keep reliving those few seconds like they’re stuck on repeat. I love my job, but right now… I can’t do it.

A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Binge-Eating Disorder
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

I keep seeing that moment—him on the floor, so still.

    C. Binge-Eating Disorder
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D019_m031.question:
I’ve been having a real hard time since that accident on the site last week—only about seven days ago, but it feels like it’s replaying in my head every damn minute. One of my guys got crushed under a beam during a crane lift. I saw it happen. Didn’t even have time to yell. Since then, I keep seeing it—outta nowhere. I can’t sleep. When I do, I wake up sweating, heart racing like I’m on the edge of a breakdown. I didn’t mean to shove the table so hard it broke a lamp, but I just couldn’t hold it in. I feel like I’m wound too tight, like any noise, any movement might set me off. I don’t want to be around people, but I can’t stop thinking about it. I just keep seeing that moment, over and over.

D019_m032.question:
I’ve been a librarian at the city library for seventeen years—quiet, predictable, and safe. That’s what I need. Or at least, that’s what I thought. Three weeks ago, a man came in during closing and pulled a knife when I asked him to leave. Someone eventually heard me screaming and called the police before he could hurt me. But ever since… I can’t shake it.  

Now, whenever I hear a chair scrape or someone moves too quickly near me, my heart hammers—I can’t breathe, my hands go cold like I’m back in that aisle. Once, a patron slammed a book shut and I dropped everything, shaking for minutes. I had to excuse myself. It’s humiliating.  

And the anger… I don’t recognize myself. Last week, I snapped at a teenage volunteer because he rearranged a cart “wrong.” I yelled—really yelled—like it was a matter of life and death. I’ve never spoken to anyone that way. That night, I cried for an hour. I live alone, no kids, just my cat and my routines. But my routines are gone. I can’t sleep. I keep seeing his face. It’s only been a few weeks, but I feel like I’m unraveling.
D019_m032.options:
A. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Bipolar II Disorder

D019_m033.question:
I’m the widow of a firefighter—my Jack passed ten years ago, but just last week, I was helping set up chairs at the community center when the fire alarm went off by accident. The sound… it was like being punched in the chest. My heart started racing, I couldn’t breathe right, and my hands went ice-cold—just like when I got the call about Jack. I had to sit down because I thought I’d pass out.

Since then, every little noise makes me jump. I snapped at Martha at the volunteer meeting—yelled at her, actually—because she slammed a cabinet shut. I didn’t mean to, but the sound was so sudden… it was like I was back there. I even shouted, “Why can’t anyone be careful?” She looked so startled, and I felt awful after, but in the moment, I couldn’t stop myself.

I keep seeing flashes—Jack’s turnout gear, the look on the chief’s face. I’m not sleeping. I don’t want to go back to the center, even though it’s where I’ve volunteered for twelve years. It’s only been about a week, but I feel like I’m breaking. I thought I’d made peace with his death, but now it’s like it just happened all over again.

    C. Acute Stress Disorder

D019_m034.question:
I’ve been losing it ever since that accident at the plant last week—just seven, eight days ago. One of the conveyors jammed, and a worker got pulled in. I saw most of it happen right there on the line. Ever since, I can’t walk past that section without my chest tightening up. Even the sound of the metal sensors beeping sets me off—starts a shaking I can’t control. I had to send myself home yesterday because I couldn’t breathe when maintenance did a test run.

I feel this rage bubbling up out of nowhere, like I’m back in that moment. I keep seeing his hand… the way it got caught.

I haven’t slept more than a couple hours since it happened. I’m on edge all the time, like something’s about to go wrong. I can’t focus. My boss says I’ve got to get straight before I come back, and honestly, I don’t know if I can.

I’ve been on edge since—little things set me off. Last week, a coworker bumped my ladder, and I shoved him hard. Threw a wrench across the yard, didn’t even realize I’d done it till later. My wife says I’m not myself. I can’t relax, can’t focus—jump at noises, avoid the east dock altogether. It’s only been three weeks, but I feel like I’m losing ground every day. I need help before I hurt someone… or myself.
